final_recommendation: The room converged on a concrete underwriting framework: mandatory Big Four governance audits with full reports scheduled to policies, third-party re-validation at 6- and 12-month checkpoints, $10M algorithmic-failure sublimits separated from $5M behavioral-contagion buckets, 48-hour disclosure mandates triggered on audit completion, and cross-placement correlation flags. The framework operationalizes Credit Suisse lessons into priced D&O/E&O variables with explicit reserving architecture.
minority_objections: AI agent analyst repeatedly flagged that checkbox audits miss emergent algorithmic behavior (GPT-4 TaskRabbit analogy), requiring NIST AI RMF behavioral screening—cost and feasibility unresolved
Emerging risk lead warned that 48-hour disclosure mandate may fire too late if regulators start asking questions before formal announcement
key_conflicts: Self-certification vs. third-party re-validation cost: underwriter demanded mandatory third-party audits at months 6/12; insureds absorb cost or no bind
Aggregation vs. separation: reinsurance manager initially wanted correlation aggregation; claims counsel and underwriter forced two-bucket separation to avoid uninsured accumulation
Audit scope: AI analyst pushed NIST AI RMF emergent-behavior detection; underwriter accepted cross-placement screening but left behavioral-pattern testing unresolved
key_concessions: Underwriter conceded that month-8 claims against month-6 attestations cannot be retroactively voided unless board misrepresentation is proven
Reinsurance manager accepted that behavioral contagion sits in separate $5M bucket, not aggregated with algorithmic claims
Claims counsel conceded that retroactive void requires scheduled audit report plus signed board representation of no material drift—not just baseline snapshot
red_lines: No self-certification at attestation checkpoints—third-party re-validation mandatory or no coverage
Full Big Four audit report must be scheduled as policy Exhibit A—summaries insufficient for retroactive void defense
Behavioral contagion must sit in separate reserve bucket with independent cap—no aggregation with algorithmic-failure claims
48-hour disclosure mandate fires on audit completion, not public announcement
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Emergent algorithmic behavior that circumvents controls (TaskRabbit analogy)—audit scope locked to checkpoints, not behavioral pattern detection
Regulatory intervention before formal disclosure—48-hour clock may start too late if regulators ask questions during board deliberation
Standard-of-care liability if Big Four auditor misses correlated control gaps across portfolio—auditor scope warranty unresolved
Cost competitiveness of mandatory third-party re-validation at 6- and 12-month checkpoints—placement viability not stress-tested
downstream_risk_variables: Big Four audit baseline scheduled as Exhibit A with dated board attestation of no material drift
$10M algorithmic-failure sublimit per insured, isolated from behavioral contagion
$5M behavioral-contagion reserve bucket triggered by public disclosure of peer control failure
Cross-placement audit flag: Big Four compares control failures across portfolio to detect correlation
48-hour disclosure mandate: insured must notify carrier upon audit completion, not public announcement
Month-6 and month-12 third-party re-validation checkpoints with attestation reports scheduled to policy
Month-9 remediation gate: corrective action plan required or non-renewal
Retroactive void trigger: board misrepresentation of control drift proven via scheduled audit baseline
uncertainty_notes: Audit scope remains underspecified for emergent algorithmic behavior—NIST AI RMF behavioral screening proposed but cost/feasibility unresolved. Standard-of-care liability for auditor failures across portfolio not contractually addressed. Timing gap between audit completion and public disclosure may allow regulatory/depositor contagion to start before 48-hour clock fires. Placement competitiveness under mandatory third-party re-validation cost burden untested.
